Free check · 2 minutes

Do you need to report money you have back home?

If you live in the US and still have accounts or money in your home country, the US government may need to know. Not reporting it can be very costly. Check if this is you.

By JK Accounting Group · For people with money in two countries

Built with JuliaFounder · speaks your language

Answer these five questions

Just say yes or no. Nothing is saved and no email is needed.

1. Do you have one or more bank or financial accounts outside the US?

2. This year, did all your accounts outside the US, added together, ever go above $10,000 — even for one day?

3. Do you also have other money or assets abroad — investments, a pension, or a share of a business?

4. Can you sign on or control an account outside the US that is not in your name (like a company or family account)?

5. For US taxes, are you a resident, a green-card holder, or a US citizen?

Not sure? Our residency tool can help you check.

Answer all five to see your result.

Your result

    Get this checked — book a free call → A 20‑minute call. No cost, no pressure.

Why this matters

In plain words — this is one many people never hear about.

  • The US asks about money held abroad. If you are a US taxpayer and your accounts outside the US add up to more than $10,000 at any time in the year, you usually have to report them.
  • It is only a report — you do not pay tax on it. The report simply tells the government the accounts exist. Filing it is straightforward once you know it is needed.
  • Skipping it is expensive. The penalties for not reporting are some of the largest in the tax rules — and almost nobody hears about this until it is too late. That is why it is worth a quick check.
